verevon.gap: No space_ref in cost-core; only an org budget_exceeded hard stop; token figures suppressed (Session Core reports 0).
verevon.strengths: Org hard stop is surfaced honestly as a refusal.

clusters.benefit: Multi-agent rooms and agent computers multiply cost; owners need attribution per room/agent.
clusters.approach: Model Plane cost-core: tag usage with space_ref and agent binding; Frontend room spend panel; per-Space allowance.
clusters.rationale: Needed before multi-agent rooms scale.

clusters.name: Admin governance of agents (allow/block, licence and plan gating)
clusters.description: Admins allow or block agent apps, scope availability by policy, gate by licence/plan, and users see why they cannot add an agent.

bestInClass.why: Explicit allow/block and reasons surfaced to users (REA q4); Slack (slack-product-surface-097) DOC.

clusters.mechanism: Org policy per agent app; per-group availability; client messaging when blocked.

verevon.gap: Org installations registry exists (presence, not authority); no allow/block policy per agent definition visible in baseline.
verevon.strengths: Room-level owner/manager gate for create/bind.

clusters.benefit: Enterprise control.
clusters.approach: Control policy on agent definitions.
clusters.rationale: Small addition.

clusters.name: AI labelling, citations and feedback on agent answers
clusters.description: Agent output carries AI labels and citations to sources; thumbs feedback with reason chips; stop-generating; admin evaluation dashboards.

bestInClass.why: Consistent AI labels, openable citations, feedback with reasons and stop on every surface (REA q4); Grok Bot (grokbot-agent-product-151) has the clearest reason chips.

clusters.mechanism: Disclaimer label per agent message; citation chips open source; feedback {thumb, reason: not asked|inaccurate|low quality|too slow, comment}.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; check SpaceRoomTimeline for feedback/citations on agent turns.

clusters.benefit: Trust and quality signal.
clusters.approach: Frontend + Model Plane feedback endpoint; citations from Data v2 retrieval.
clusters.rationale: Cheap and common.

clusters.name: Room-behaviour evaluation suites for agents
clusters.description: Benchmarks that grade how agents behave inside rooms: reply in the right thread, notify exactly the right person, stay silent when not addressed, attribute correctly.

bestInClass.why: Runs the real product process tree per task with pinned prompts, used as release regression (SRC q5). QM (qm-product-086) runs multiplayer scenarios on real Slack.

clusters.mechanism: Task containers with roster manifest, scripted human actors, assertions on placement/notification/silence, LLM judge.

verevon.gap: No baseline record.

clusters.benefit: Prevents regressions as rooms gain multi-agent features.
clusters.approach: Test harness against gateway + Model Plane with synthetic members.
clusters.rationale: Engineering safeguard.

clusters.name: Headless one-shot agent task runner
clusters.description: Scripts run one prepared agent task with a deadline and receive one JSON result line and a precise exit code.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q4).

clusters.mechanism: Versioned task contract; deadline; single JSON line result.

verevon.gap: No baseline record.

clusters.benefit: CI and automation integration.
clusters.approach: Gateway API for one-shot runs.
clusters.rationale: Developer convenience.

clusters.name: Agent-proposed configuration changes reviewed by the owner
clusters.description: An agent cannot create agents or attach channels itself; it opens a typed proposal delivered privately to its owner as a prefilled dialog; nothing changes until the owner saves.

bestInClass.why: Only source (SRC q4): strict allowlisted schema, dedupe and a bounded queue over a private agent-to-owner channel.

clusters.mechanism: Agent CLI emits typed requests; client parses with an allowlist schema; owner sees a prefilled dialog; save performs the change with owner authority.

verevon.gap: No baseline record.
verevon.strengths: Matches the rule that decisions authorising future agent behaviour come from outside the agent.

clusters.benefit: Agents can help configure the workspace safely.
clusters.approach: Application proposal object; Frontend review dialog.
clusters.rationale: Nice pattern, low urgency.

clusters.name: Private assistant surface beside the room, with escalation to the group
clusters.description: A personal assistant in a side panel or summoned by hotkey that knows what you are looking at; private prompts stay private and can be escalated into the shared conversation.

bestInClass.why: Explicit private-vs-group model with an escalate-to-group dialog (DOC q4); Slack (slack-product-surface-080, -093) adds split view and global hotkey summon.

clusters.mechanism: Side panel bound to current context; private session; 'share to group' posts a reviewed copy into the room.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; Verevon has /chat personal threads but no side panel inside a Space.

clusters.benefit: Lets people consult an agent without noise in the room.
clusters.approach: Frontend split view reusing /chat with Space context; share-to-room uses review-then-share.
clusters.risks: Context leakage into the private panel is fine; leakage out needs review.
clusters.rationale: Natural home for personal agents inside rooms.
